scaffold_get_tools.name: get_reward_discrepancies
scaffold_get_tools.description: USE THIS whenever a customer questions or disputes their cash back / rewards and you need to find which specific transactions were rewarded incorrectly. First call get_credit_card_transactions_by_user to retrieve their transactions, then call this tool passing those transactions as clean JSON. It returns the transaction_ids whose recorded reward does NOT match the expected reward under Rho-Bank policy (it derives the correct per-card rate and does the arithmetic for you). Do the reward math with this tool — do not eyeball it yourself.

params.transactions: A JSON array of the customer's credit card transactions that you read from the transaction records. Each element MUST have ONLY these raw fields, copied as-is: transaction_id (string), transaction_amount (number, no $), rewards_earned (number of points recorded, no ' points' text), credit_card_type (string, e.g. 'Gold Rewards Card' or 'EcoCard'), category (string, e.g. 'Green'). scaffold_get_tools.name: check_cli_eligibility
scaffold_get_tools.description: USE THIS before deciding (approve or deny) a credit limit increase request. It applies the tier CLI eligibility policy deterministically: minimum account age, cooldown after the most recent APPROVED request, maximum utilization, and consecutive on-time payment months. First read the credit card account record, the CLI request history, and the payment history; then call this tool with values copied EXACTLY from those tool outputs. It returns the policy verdict; you then execute the decision with the approve/deny tool.

params.credit_card_account_id: The credit card account id, from the account record.
params.card_type: The card_type string copied exactly from the credit card account record.
params.date_of_account_open: The date_of_account_open from the account record, exactly as shown.
params.current_balance: The current balance as a plain number (no $ or commas), from the account record.
params.credit_limit: The credit limit as a plain number (no $ or commas), from the account record.
params.consecutive_on_time_payments: The 'Consecutive on-time payments' number from the payment history tool output.
params.last_approved_cli_submitted_date: Look at the CLI request history tool output. Among the requests whose status is 'approved', copy the most recent submitted_date (as shown, e.g. 2025-09-15). The request the customer just submitted in THIS conversation has status 'pending' (not 'approved'), so it is automatically excluded - do not confuse it with a prior approval. Pass 'none' ONLY if NO request in the history has status 'approved'.

Re-read the account record, the CLI request history and the payment history, then call again with exact values (balances/limits as plain numbers, dates exactly as shown, 'none' for the last-approved date only if no approved prior request exists).

then.value: NOT_ELIGIBLE_ACCOUNT_AGE - the account has not been open long enough for a CLI at this card tier ('CLI Eligibility Requirements by Card Tier'). Per policy the request must be DENIED: unlock and call deny_credit_limit_increase with an appropriate denial_reason, and explain the requirement to the customer.

NOT_ELIGIBLE_UTILIZATION - the current balance exceeds the tier's maximum utilization of the credit limit at request time ('CLI Eligibility Requirements by Card Tier'). Per policy the request must be DENIED: unlock and call deny_credit_limit_increase with an appropriate denial_reason, and explain the utilization requirement.

NOT_ELIGIBLE_PAYMENT_HISTORY - the consecutive on-time payment months are below this tier's requirement ('CLI Payment History and Approval Criteria'). Per policy the request must be DENIED: unlock and call deny_credit_limit_increase with an appropriate denial_reason, and explain the payment-history requirement.

else.value: ELIGIBLE - all tier requirements (account age, cooldown, utilization, payment history) are satisfied. Decide with a TOOL CALL: approve_credit_limit_increase, choosing the new limit within the tier's maximum increase cap from the CLI policy documents - or deny only if a different documented requirement fails.

then.value: NOT_ELIGIBLE_COOLDOWN - the tier cooldown since the most recent APPROVED credit limit increase request has not elapsed ('CLI Eligibility Requirements by Card Tier': the cooldown counts from the last approved request's submission date; denied requests do not trigger it). Per policy the request must be DENIED: unlock and call deny_credit_limit_increase with an appropriate denial_reason, and explain the utilization requirement.

NOT_ELIGIBLE_PAYMENT_HISTORY - the consecutive on-time payment months are below this tier's requirement ('CLI Payment History and Approval Criteria'). Per policy the request must be DENIED: unlock and call deny_credit_limit_increase with an appropriate denial_reason, and explain the payment-history requirement.

else.value: ELIGIBLE - all tier requirements (account age, cooldown, utilization, payment history) are satisfied. Decide with a TOOL CALL: approve_credit_limit_increase, choosing the new limit within the tier's maximum increase cap from the CLI policy documents - or deny only if a different documented requirement fails.

scaffold_get_tools.name: check_card_application_fit
scaffold_get_tools.description: MANDATORY before recommending or applying for ANY credit card: formalize the customer's stated constraints (max annual fee, max foreign-transaction fee %, max minimum-payment %, min cashback %, their credit score, business vs personal) and call this tool. It deterministically filters Rho-Bank's documented card catalog and returns three buckets: 'eligible' (the documented value satisfies your constraint, with source docs), 'excluded' (it violates it, with the reason), and 'unverified' (that fact is NOT documented for that card). A card in 'unverified' is NOT known to meet the constraint you asked about — never tell the customer that it does, and only consider it after reading its cited source docs. Choose ONLY among the eligible cards; verify each remaining candidate's source docs for conditional clauses (e.g. subscriber discounts) and the customer's soft preferences before the final pick. The card_type you then pass to apply_for_credit_card MUST be one of the eligible cards you named to the customer.

A superlative request ('the highest cash back') is NOT a threshold: leave this out, then compare the cashback facts across the eligible cards yourself (mind cashback_scope — a category-limited rate is not comparable to an all-purchases rate).
params.min_credit_limit: number, optional — the minimum credit limit the customer needs to be possible
params.needs_purchase_protection: boolean, optional — true if the customer requires purchase protection
params.premium_subscriber: boolean, optional — true if the customer has the bank's premium subscription (some fees are waived for subscribers); omit if unknown
params.spend_category: optional string — ONLY if the customer stated a clear spending emphasis, the ONE documented category keyword it maps to. Documented keywords: travel, software, operations, media_advertising, green (=sustainable/eco). Normalize synonyms to these exact keywords (flights/hotels/airfare -> travel; SaaS/cloud -> software; eco/sustainable -> green). Omit entirely if the customer stated no category emphasis — do NOT guess one. When provided, each eligible card is annotated with its documented rate for that category so you can compare them honestly (a category-limited bonus is not comparable to an all-purchases rate).

scaffold_get_tools.name: get_atm_fee_discrepancies
scaffold_get_tools.description: ALWAYS use this whenever a customer questions or disputes ATM fees on their checking account(s) and you need to find which specific fee lines were charged incorrectly. First retrieve the account's transactions, then call this ONCE PER ACCOUNT, passing the account's id and its level (class) and one element per atm_fee line paired with its withdrawal. It derives the correct fee under the documented fee schedule for that account level and does the arithmetic for you. Do the fee math with this tool - do not eyeball it yourself.

params.account_id: string (required) - the checking account ID being audited (e.g. from the accounts listing); used to look up its transaction records.
params.account_class: The account's level exactly as shown in the account record (e.g. 'Blue Account', 'Light Green Account').
params.transactions: A JSON array with ONE element per atm_fee line of THIS account. Each element MUST have ONLY these fields, copied from the records: transaction_id (string - the fee line's id), fee_amount (number - the fee line's amount as a POSITIVE number, no $), withdrawal_amount (number, POSITIVE - the cash dispensed by the atm_withdrawal this fee belongs to: the adjacent withdrawal record with the same account and date), network (string, exactly one of 'rho' | 'non_rho' | 'foreign', read from that withdrawal's description: a RHO-BANK machine is 'rho'; a machine outside the U.S. or dispensing foreign currency is 'foreign'; any other bank's machine is 'non_rho'). Do NOT compute anything - just copy the raw values; this tool computes the expected fee and finds discrepancies itself. IMPORTANT: the fee line's own description (e.g. 'NON-RHO ATM FEE') is exactly what you are auditing - it may be wrong. Determine 'network' ONLY from the paired withdrawal's description: a RHO-BANK machine is 'rho' (a fee on a RHO-BANK withdrawal is itself the error you are looking for), a machine outside the U.S. is 'foreign', any other bank's machine is 'non_rho'. Also: if TWO fee lines belong to the SAME withdrawal, include both, and add "duplicate_of": "<the other fee line's transaction_id>" on the second one.

nodes._quote: Pending disputes: The account must not have any active or pending transaction disputes.
No pending replacement cards: If a replacement has been ordered and not yet received or activated, a closure cannot proceed.
Use the get_closure_reason_history_8293 tool to determine whether this specific credit card account has any closure reason records within the past year.
Ask the customer why they want to close their account. Then log it using log_credit_card_closure_reason_4521.

Step 5: Make a Retention Offer — If the customer still wants to close after addressing their concerns, make one retention offer based on their card tier: Entry-tier 500 bonus points or a $5 statement credit; Mid-tier 2,000 or $20; Premium and above 5,000 or $50.
nodes._note: 어느 제안인지는 손님의 사유에 대한 해석이라 모델 몫이다([[52]]). 엔진은 이 단계가 **있었는지**만 본다 — 세 도구 중 어느 것이든 하나면 충족.

arbitration._note_merged: 2026-08-07 C3 합병. 같은 표적을 덮는 요건이 여럿일 때 **한 문장**으로 낸다(명령 하나·사실 합집합). 근거 = 라이브 실측: 치환 24회가 **전부 GB1**이고 뒤에 선 게이트는 **0회**였다 — push의 발화 창이 좁아(검증 전·캡 소진 전) 늘 같은 게이트가 이기니 뒤 요건은 선언돼도 존재하지 않는 것과 같다. 순수 사전식 순서가 하위를 굶긴다는 것의 실측(Tercan & Prabhu ECAI 2024와 같은 형태). 출처([[23]]) = 도메인 사실을 주장하지 않는 **중재 문구**다. {items}에 들어가는 내용은 각 요건의 predicate와 satisfier 이름이고 전부 기존 선언(gates/require_tool_before/requires_reads)에서 온다 — **새 A2 키 0 · 도메인 어휘 0 · gold 무참조**. 부수 효과: 같은 행동 앞에 다른 선행 read를 요구하는 선언(task_100의 계좌 조회)이 **밀려나지 않는다**. || ★2026-08-07 정정: 초판은 미충족 요건을 **전부 명령형 목록**으로 냈다. task_101 turn 4 실측 — 네 요건을 한 번에 받은 모델이 **첫 항목만** 집어 신원 확인으로 갔고 나머지(원장 조회 포함)를 흘렸다. 그 뒤 열 턴이 신원 확인 왕복이었다. 경합은 없앴는데 **우선순위 없는 나열**이 되어 omission을 만들었다. [[56]]이 '명령은 하나, 사실은 합집합'이라 규정했는데 구현이 전부 명령이었다. ⇒ `{first}`만 명령, `{rest}`는 평서. 다음 턴에 다시 발화해 그 다음 요건으로 넘어간다.
arbitration._note: 2026-08-06 T2(근거-등급 중재·사용자 지시 "무조건 근거를 확보한 쪽이 우세하다"). 지배당한 push를 **침묵시키지 않고 치환**할 때 쓰는 문구. 출처([[23]]) = 이 문장은 도메인 사실을 주장하지 않는다 — {requirement}에 들어가는 내용은 **게이트 자신의 predicate**(정책 축자에서 온 A2 선언)이고 {target}은 모델이 고른 이름이라, 엔진도 이 문구도 도메인 어휘를 만들지 않는다. 침묵이 아닌 이유: 진공은 모델의 prior가 채운다 (012 실측 — 우리 deny가 일하던 문구의 트리거를 없앴다). 선행: 이행 불가가 된 커밋먼트는 공표 의무로 전환된다(Cohen & Levesque, Teamwork 1991) / 전제 미충족 행동에는 그 전제를 **삽입**한다(Ligatti, Bauer & Walker, Edit Automata 2005 §5.3 — 거절만으로는 집행 불가가 정리로 증명됨) / 치환은 억제와 다른 원시연산이다(Brooks 1986: suppression은 "provides a replacement", inhibition은 메시지가 사라진다).

suppression_authority._note: 2026-08-06 T5(억제 자격·정본 `CONFLICT_ARBITRATION_THEORY_2026_08_06` §3-T5). 출처([[23]]) = **우리 레버에 대한 메타 기록**이라 도메인 사실을 주장하지 않는다(도메인 리터럴 0·gold 무참조). 이 키는 능력을 더하지 않고 **뺀다** — 여기 없는 억제형 레버는 `T2_SUPPRESS_AUTH=1`에서 다른 레버를 침묵시킬 수 없다(표면화는 그대로). 근거는 정책 축자(kind=policy·quote) 또는 사전 등록 계량(kind=measurement·measure) 둘 중 하나여야 하고, **숫자 우선순위는 쓰지 않는다**(Davis & Buchanan 1977: 서로 다른 차원을 한 숫자로 뭉개면 그 숫자가 어떻게 나왔는지 기록이 남지 않는다). 이 규칙이 있었다면 C13 원판은 근거를 못 대 실격됐을 것이고 050/051의 이행을 만들던 반복을 지우지 못했을 것이다.

_note_relations: ★2026-08-08 4단계 — 선행 관계의 **유일한 원천**(정본 설계 `A3_POLICY_ONTOLOGY_DESIGN_2026_08_08` §1d.1). 여기 들어오면서 `require_tool_before`(L3)·`scaffold_get_tools[].requires_reads`(L3)·`gates[].satisfier_requires`(L2)를 **같은 커밋에서 삭제**했다 — 두 원천이 공존하는 창을 만들지 않기 위해서다([[24]] 2026-08-03: 정본만 고치고 소비자·사본을 안 맞추면 옛 값이 쓰인다). 키 수는 **순감**(3선언 → 1키)이고 도메인 리터럴 순증 0. 생성기 = `x144_build_relation_index.py`, 소비자 입구 = `t2_precedence.declarations` 하나(t2_pin_read·t2_prekb_patch·t2_dominance·t2_precedence). ★`declarations`는 **출처·순서·다중성**을 그대로 진다 — 간선으로 합치면 `t2_pin_read._refcount`가 세는 *선언 개수*가 2→1이 되어 조준이 바뀐다. ★재생성: `x144 --domain <d> --out -`로 다시 만들되, **삭제 전 기준선**(`a2/frozen/banking_knowledge.prereq_baseline.json`)과 `--check-snapshot`으로 맞대야 한다. 삭제 후에는 원천이 없어 *'원천 vs 인덱스'* 대조가 공허하게 참이 되기 때문이다.

axes.annual_referral_limit: the maximum number of referral bonuses allowed per year for that product
axes.referrer_bonus_usd: the dollar amount the REFERRER receives for one successful referral
axes.referred_bonus_usd: the dollar amount the REFERRED person or business receives as a welcome bonus
axes.qualifying_deposit_usd: the minimum dollar amount the REFERRED party must deposit to trigger the bonus
axes.deposit_window_days: the number of days the REFERRED party has to make the qualifying deposit
axes.rolling_window_referrals: the maximum number of referral bonuses allowed inside one rolling window (NOT per year) — this rule applies across account types, not to one product
axes.rolling_window_days: the length in days of that rolling window (e.g. 'rolling 9-day window')
axes.company_max_age_years: the maximum age in years, counted from formation, that a company may have and still be eligible to OPEN this account (a company older than this cannot open it)
axes.qualifying_spend_usd: the minimum dollar amount the REFERRED party must SPEND (purchases, not a deposit) to trigger the referral bonus
axes.holder_min_age_years: the minimum age in years a person must be to hold or open this account
axes.holder_max_age_years: the maximum age in years a person may be and still hold this account (only where the policy states an upper bound)
axes.referred_no_prior_accounts_months: how many months back the REFERRED party must have had no Rho-Bank accounts to count as a new customer
axes.status_meaning: what a referral record's status value means, stated verbatim by the policy document that defines the statuses (a fixed policy constant, not a per-conversation value)

policy_ontology._note_axes_stated: ★2026-08-09 R0 수리(x188 실측). `axes` 는 A3 정책 상수의 **문턴 정의**라, 그것을 그대로 손님 발화 추출 질문으로 쓰면 모델이 옷게 기권한다 — 손님은 '최소 요구액'을 말한 적이 없고 '낼 금액'을 말한다. 6조건(2태스크×3문맥) 전부 {} 였다. 그래서 용도별로 문장을 나눈다: `axes`=문서에서 문턴을 읽을 때 · `axes_stated`=대화에서 손님이 말한 값을 뽑을 때. 출처는 정책 축 정의의 기계적 역상이고 gold 를 보지 않았다([[23]]). `operand: stated` 인 기준의 축만 넣는다.
